title: Smaller Pumpkins, Bigger Questions: England’s Halloween Harvest Struggles
subtitle: As a record-breaking drought impacts the size of this year's crop, experts suggest it is time to rethink our Halloween traditions.

summary.en: England is facing a shortage of large pumpkins this Halloween due to a severe, long-lasting drought. Because pumpkins are mostly water, the lack of rain has made it difficult for farmers to grow them to their usual size. Experts note that while the harvest is smaller, the vegetables are still healthy and store well. Some leaders in the food industry are now encouraging people to move away from large carving pumpkins. They suggest choosing smaller, more flavorful squashes that can be eaten rather than thrown away.
summary.zh: 英國今年因長期嚴重的乾旱，面臨大型南瓜短缺的問題。由於南瓜主要由水分組成，降雨不足導致農民難以將其種植至往常的尺寸。專家指出，雖然收成較小，但這些蔬菜依然健康且易於保存。部分食品產業領袖正鼓勵民眾改變對大型雕刻南瓜的依賴，建議選擇體積較小、風味更佳的南瓜，以便食用而非丟棄。

paragraphs.en: As Halloween approaches, many families in England are preparing to decorate their homes with carved pumpkins. However, this year, those looking for the biggest, roundest pumpkins may be disappointed. According to The Guardian, a severe drought—a long period of time with very little rain—has significantly affected the harvest. Farmers have struggled to provide enough water for their crops, leading to pumpkins that are much smaller than in previous years.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著萬聖節即將到來，英國許多家庭正準備用雕刻南瓜來裝飾住家。然而，今年想找最大、最圓南瓜的人可能會感到失望。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，嚴重的乾旱——即長時間缺乏降雨——已對收成造成重大影響。農民難以提供作物足夠的水分，導致南瓜比往年小得多。

paragraphs.en: This news follows earlier reports about the difficult growing season in 2026. Because pumpkins are made of about 90% water, they need a large amount of moisture to grow to their full size. The Guardian reports that this year could be the worst harvest on record. While some gardeners have tried new methods to help their crops grow in heavy clay soil, the lack of rain has made it very hard to get the desired results.
paragraphs.zh: 這則消息是在先前關於二〇二六年艱困生長季的報導之後傳出的。由於南瓜約有百分之九十是水分，它們需要大量濕氣才能長到完整尺寸。《衛報》指出，今年可能是史上最慘澹的收成。儘管有些園丁嘗試了新方法來幫助作物在黏重的土壤中生長，但缺乏雨水使得獲得理想成果變得非常困難。

paragraphs.en: Guy Barter, the chief horticulturalist at the Royal Horticultural Society, explained that pumpkins are usually good at surviving dry weather. However, he noted that the extreme heat and lack of water this year pushed them to their limit. He added that the heat caused the fruits to ripen earlier than usual. On the positive side, the pumpkins that were harvested have hard rinds and are in good condition, meaning they should store well for those who still plan to carve them.
paragraphs.zh: 英國皇家園藝學會（Royal Horticultural Society）的首席園藝專家蓋伊·巴特（Guy Barter）解釋說，南瓜通常很能適應乾燥氣候。然而，他指出今年極端的高溫與缺水已將它們推向極限。他補充說，高溫導致果實比往常更早成熟。從正面來看，收成的南瓜外皮堅硬且狀況良好，這意味著對於仍打算雕刻它們的人來說，這些南瓜應該能妥善保存。

paragraphs.en: While the smaller size of the pumpkins is a practical problem for those wanting to carve traditional faces, it has also started a wider conversation about waste. Guy Singh-Watson, the founder of the organic vegetable company Riverford, believes that the current situation is a chance to change how we celebrate. He pointed out that growing a large, watery vegetable just to throw it away after one night of Halloween is not environmentally friendly. He argued that growing any crop has an environmental cost, and creating a large amount of waste without feeding anyone does not make much sense.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然南瓜尺寸變小對於想雕刻傳統鬼臉的人來說是個實際問題，但也引發了關於浪費的廣泛討論。有機蔬菜公司 Riverford 的創辦人蓋伊·辛格-華生（Guy Singh-Watson）認為，當前的情況是一個改變慶祝方式的契機。他指出，種植一種水分充足的大型蔬菜，卻只為了在萬聖節過後丟棄，並不符合環保原則。他主張，種植任何作物都有環境成本，在沒有餵飽任何人的情況下製造大量垃圾並不合理。

paragraphs.en: Instead of focusing on giant pumpkins, Singh-Watson suggests that people should return to older traditions. In the 17th century, before pumpkins became the standard, people in Britain carved root vegetables like turnips and mangelwurzels to mark the ancient festival of Samhain. These carved vegetables were used to represent spirits and were thought to keep evil away. Singh-Watson suggests that today’s families could paint faces on smaller, colorful squashes instead of carving them. This would allow people to use the vegetables for decoration first, and then cook them into delicious soups or meals afterward.
paragraphs.zh: 辛格-華生建議人們不要執著於巨型南瓜，而應回歸更古老的傳統。在十七世紀，南瓜尚未成為標準裝飾之前，英國人會雕刻蕪菁和飼料甜菜來紀念古老的薩溫節（Samhain）。這些雕刻過的蔬菜被用來代表靈魂，並被認為能驅邪。辛格-華生建議，現代家庭可以改在較小、色彩繽紛的南瓜品種上彩繪鬼臉，而不是進行雕刻。這能讓民眾先將蔬菜用於裝飾，之後再烹調成美味的湯品或餐點。

paragraphs.en: This approach offers a way to enjoy the season while being more mindful of resources. There is an extraordinary variety of squashes available, such as crown prince, red onion, and sweet lightning varieties. These vegetables come in many different shapes and colors, offering just as much beauty for decorations as a traditional pumpkin, but with much more flavor. By choosing these options, consumers can celebrate the abundance of the autumn season without the guilt of throwing away food.
paragraphs.zh: 這種做法提供了一種既能享受節日，又能更珍惜資源的方式。市面上有種類繁多的南瓜可供選擇，例如皇冠王子（crown prince）、紅洋蔥（red onion）和甜閃電（sweet lightning）等品種。這些蔬菜擁有許多不同的形狀與顏色，作為裝飾品時與傳統南瓜一樣美觀，且風味更佳。透過選擇這些選項，消費者既能慶祝秋季的豐收，也不必因為丟棄食物而感到愧疚。

paragraphs.en: Despite the challenges, the tradition of Halloween remains strong. While the pumpkins on front porches might be smaller this year, they still represent a long-standing custom. Experts suggest that the current drought is a reminder to be more flexible with our holiday habits. Whether people choose to find smaller pumpkins or switch to other types of winter squashes, the focus this year seems to be shifting toward sustainability. As the season continues, many are looking at this as an opportunity to appreciate the natural variety of the harvest rather than focusing only on the size of a single vegetable. As the weather turns colder and we move toward the end of the year, these smaller, more flavorful squashes will likely become a common sight on dinner tables across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管面臨挑戰，萬聖節的傳統依然穩固。雖然今年門廊上的南瓜可能較小，但它們仍代表著一項悠久的習俗。專家建議，目前的乾旱提醒我們在節日習慣上應更具彈性。無論人們選擇尋找較小的南瓜，還是改用其他類型的冬南瓜，今年的焦點似乎正轉向永續發展。隨著季節更迭，許多人將此視為欣賞自然收成多樣性的機會，而非僅僅執著於單一蔬菜的尺寸。隨著天氣轉冷並邁向年底，這些體積較小、風味更豐富的南瓜，很可能會成為全國餐桌上常見的景象。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To force someone or something to reach a difficult or extreme limit.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 迫使（某人或某物）達到極限。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作物理上的「推」，這裡指環境因素使作物達到承受極限。文中：However, he noted that the extreme heat and lack of water this year pushed them to their limit.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To celebrate or observe an important event or period.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 慶祝或紀念（某個節日或重要時刻）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（記號）或動詞（做記號），這裡指慶祝節日。文中：In the 17th century, before pumpkins became the standard, people in Britain carved root vegetables like turnips and mangelwurzels to mark the ancient festival of Samhain.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To change into a different state or condition.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「轉彎」，這裡指天氣的變化。文中：As the weather turns colder and we move toward the end of the year, these smaller, more flavorful squashes will likely become a common sight on dinner tables across the country.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason why this year's pumpkins have reached maturity earlier than usual?

options.A: The use of new gardening methods in heavy clay soil.
options.B: The combination of extreme heat and a lack of water.
options.C: The shift in planting schedules compared to 2026.
options.D: The specific variety of seeds planted by farmers this season.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，Guy Barter 明確指出極端的高溫（extreme heat）與缺水導致南瓜比往常更早成熟。選項 A 雖然提到了新方法，但那是為了對抗缺水，而非導致早熟的原因；選項 C 與 D 在文中並未提及是導致早熟的因素，屬於無中生有的干擾選項。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the environmental impact of traditional Halloween pumpkin carving?

options.A: It is considered sustainable because pumpkins are biodegradable.
options.B: It is criticized because the process of carving damages the soil.
options.C: It is viewed as wasteful because the pumpkins are often discarded without being eaten.
options.D: It is becoming more environmentally friendly as pumpkins get smaller.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，Guy Singh-Watson 批評將巨大的蔬菜僅為了萬聖節裝飾而種植，最後卻直接丟棄，這是不環保的行為，因為種植農作物本身有環境成本。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 誤解了文章提到的「泥土」問題，那是種植困難而非裝飾問題；選項 D 雖然提到南瓜變小，但文章並未說這讓傳統雕刻變得環保。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'flexible' mean in the context of holiday habits?

options.A: Physically bending or stretching an object.
options.B: Being willing to change plans or adapt to new circumstances.
options.C: Having a weak or easily broken structure.
options.D: Spending more money to ensure the holiday is perfect.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「flexible」意指人們應對氣候變遷與南瓜短缺，願意調整慶祝習慣（如改用其他瓜類或裝飾方式）。選項 A 是字面意思，在此處不適用；選項 C 與 D 皆與文中建議人們適應環境變化、追求永續性的脈絡完全無關。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the 2026 pumpkin harvest?

options.A: The drought has made it impossible to celebrate Halloween in England.
options.B: Farmers need to switch permanently to growing root vegetables.
options.C: The small harvest is an opportunity to embrace sustainable and varied ways of celebrating.
options.D: The quality of pumpkins this year is poor, making them unsuitable for any purpose.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文雖由南瓜歉收的負面消息開頭，但重點在於轉向討論如何透過改變習慣（如使用不同瓜類、減少浪費）來落實永續生活。選項 A 過於誇大；選項 B 僅是建議之一，非核心主旨；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章提到這些南瓜依然適合雕刻且品質良好，並非完全無用。
